test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: maths
question:
If the digits of a two digit number is reversed, then the number is decreased by 36. Which of the following is correct regarding the number ?

I. The difference of the digits is 4.

II. The value of number can be 84.

III. Number is always a composite number.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between a two-digit number and its reverse is always 9 × (Difference of digits).

9 × (x − y) = 36 ⇒ x − y = 4. (Statement I is correct)

Possible numbers (x − y = 4): 40, 51, 62, 73, 84, 95.

Since 84 is in the list, Statement II is correct. Since 73 is prime, Statement III is incorrect.

**∴ The correct answer is I and II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: A two-digit number decreases by 36 when digits are reversed.

Let the tens digit be x and the units digit be y. Number = 10x + y.

Reversed number = 10y + x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/539180ebc48d521453bd254418507a168d6b26ab6c2a9f4f9d3cf17d60d558a6.png] 

⇒ (10x + y) − (10y + x) = 36

⇒ 9x − 9y = 36

⇒ 9(x − y) = 36

⇒ x − y = 4 (This confirms Statement I)

⇒ Possible values for (x, y) where x − y = 4 are: (4,0), (5,1), (6,2), (7,3), (8,4), (9,5).

⇒ Possible numbers: 40, 51, 62, 73, 84, 95.

⇒ Number 84 satisfies the condition (84 − 48 = 36). (This confirms Statement II)

⇒ 73 is a Prime number, so the number is not always composite. (Statement III is False)

**∴ The correct answer is I and II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Digits Property

The sum of a two-digit number and the number formed by reversing its digits is always divisible by 11. Sum = 11(x + y).

Difference of Digits Property

The difference between a two-digit number and its reverse is always divisible by 9. Difference = 9|x − y|.

Prime vs Composite Numbers

A prime number has exactly two factors (1 and itself). A composite number has more than two factors. For example, 73 is prime, whereas 51 (3 × 17) is composite.</p
